what: The data: a multiplex network of the Chilean rocky intertidal
title: Assembly of multilayer networks: trophic and non-trophic interactions
text: multiweb package includes network Kéfi et al. (2015), 106 species central Chilean rocky shore three layers: trophic links, positive non-trophic links (mostly habitat refuge provision sessile species) negative non-trophic links (mostly competition space). multiweb::readMultiplex() returns mgraph, list igraph layers; names give layers identifiers.
code: library(meweasmo) suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(igraph))  fpath <- system.file("extdata", package = "multiweb") dn <- list.files(fpath, pattern = "^Kefi2015.*\\.txt$") dn                                         # files in alphabetical order: negative, positive, trophic #> [1] "Kefi2015_chilean_NTIneg.txt" "Kefi2015_chilean_NTIpos.txt" #> [3] "Kefi2015_chilean_TI.txt" mg <- multiweb::readMultiplex(dn, types = c("Negative", "Positive", "Trophic"), fpath, skipColumn = 2) sapply(mg, ecount) #> Negative Positive  Trophic  #>     3089      172     1362

title: Assembly of multilayer networks: trophic and non-trophic interactions
text: simulating must know link -> b means layer, datasets use different conventions. matrices row species receives effect column species, readMultiplex() makes links row column. trophic layer links therefore go prey predator, meweasmo expects. Basal species incoming links: positive layer links go beneficiary species provides benefit: habitat formers, mussel Perumytilus purpuratus kelp Lessonia nigrescens, receive links. species origin positive link receives positive effect species end none, (+, 0); negative layer origin receives negative effect, (-, 0). Competition, recorded directions, becomes (-, -). write layer table (see default_layer_signs() format; defaults follow different convention): links network carry sign effect edge attribute, use effect_attr instead layer signs needed.
code: tr <- mg$Trophic head(V(tr)$name[degree(tr, mode = "in") == 0]) #> [1] "adenocystis utricularis" "ahnfeltiopsis spp."      #> [3] "benthic_diatoms"         "bryopsis_spp"            #> [5] "centroceras spp."        "ceramium spp." head(sort(degree(mg$Positive, mode = "in"), decreasing = TRUE)) #>              perumytilus purpuratus                 semimytilus algosus  #>                                  38                                  26  #>                 lessonia nigrescens                       gelidium spp.  #>                                  25                                  13  #> corallina offcinalis var. chilensis             mazzaella laminarioides  #>                                  11                                  10 layers <- data.frame(layer     = c("Trophic", "Positive", "Negative"),                      sign_from = c(-1, 1, -1),                      sign_to   = c( 1, 0,  0),                      rule      = c("trophic", "modifier", "modifier"))

title: Assembly of multilayer networks: trophic and non-trophic interactions
text: build_multilayer_assembly() shows network translated: trophic meta-web metaW, matrix M effects log extinction rate, obligate dependence matrix Dep. title: Simulation of metaweb assembly models
text: package simulates assembly ecological networks regional metaweb. Three main models implemented; first trophic theory island biogeography [2] addition secondary extinctions fixed happen defined probability. Second generalized Lotka-Volterra stochastic model. Third, multilayer version first model non-trophic interactions (mutualism, facilitation, competition) change extinction rates. Species can migrate metaweb establish ecological interactions specified metaweb. License: MIT

what: Multilayer networks: trophic and non-trophic interactions
title: Simulation of metaweb assembly models
text: metaWebNetAssemblyML() extends continuous-time assembly model multilayer networks. trophic layer defines meta-web secondary extinctions, metaWebNetAssemblyCT(); non-trophic layers change extinction rates: losing mutualist habitat provider raises extinction rate species, losing competitor lowers . Optionally, species can depend obligately others (e.g. foundation species). network can mgraph multiweb package, list igraph layers, edge list. See article Assembly multilayer networks (vignette("multilayer-assembly")) worked example Chilean rocky intertidal network Kéfi et al. (2015).
code: fpath <- system.file("extdata", package = "multiweb") dn <- list.files(fpath, pattern = "^Kefi2015.*\\.txt$") mg <- multiweb::readMultiplex(dn, types = c("Negative", "Positive", "Trophic"), fpath, skipColumn = 2)  # sign of the effect received by the species at the origin and at the end of each link layers <- data.frame(layer = c("Trophic", "Positive", "Negative"), sign_from = c(-1, 1, -1),                      sign_to = c(1, 0, 0), rule = c("trophic", "modifier", "modifier"))  r <- metaWebNetAssemblyML(mg, layers, beta = c(pos = 1, neg = 1), m = 0.1, e = 0.05, se = 0.5, time = 300)

title: Generate random parameters of a generalized Lotka-Volterra model from an adjacency matrix — generateGLVparmsFromAdj
text: type interaction read signs adjM (adjM[, j] effect species j species ): adjM[, j] < 0 adjM[j, ] > 0: predator-prey, j predator prey. strength effect prey random effect predator ef times effect prey, opposite sign. negative: competition; positive: mutualism. direction gets random strength. adjM[, j] > 0 adjM[j, ] == 0: commensalism (benefits); adjM[, j] < 0 adjM[j, ] == 0: amensalism (harmed). strengths interactions (-diagonal values) drawn according preserveInt rndType. remaining parameters depend type species, also deduced adjM: mutualistic takes part mutualistic interaction, otherwise basal resources (never predator predator-prey interaction, species j commensalism), otherwise consumer. type: Self-limitation (diagonal interaction matrix): -runif(0, 2 * selfLimAvg[k]), k 1 mutualistic, 2 basal 3 consumer species. diagonal adjM ignored. Intrinsic growth rate r: positive, runif(0, 1), basal species; negative, -runif(0, 1), consumers (need resources persist); random sign, magnitude, mutualistic species (random obligate mutualism). Migration m: runif(0, 2 * migrAvg) species. equivalent implementation R, generateGLVparmsFromAdjR(), gives results random seed.

title: Simulation of an Assembly process from a Meta-web with stochastic Generalized Lotka-Volterra dynamics — metaWebNetAssemblyGLV
text: abundance \(N_i\) species \(\) changes time according $$\frac{dN_i}{dt} = N_i \left( r_i + \sum_j A_{ij} N_j \right) + m_i$$ \(r_i\) intrinsic growth rate (r), \(A_{ij}\) interaction matrix (metaW) \(m_i\) constant immigration rate (m). model integrated tau-leap method [1]: time divided steps size tau, step abundance species changes Poisson distributed number individuals mean abs(rate) * tau, rate right hand side equation ; change positive rate > 0 negative otherwise. Abundances truncated zero. Species updated sequentially within step, species uses already updated abundances species . signs interaction matrix define type interaction species j: metaW[, j] < 0 metaW[j, ] > 0: predator-prey, j predator prey. metaW[, j] > 0 metaW[j, ] > 0: mutualism. metaW[, j] < 0 metaW[j, ] < 0: competition. metaW[, j] != 0 metaW[j, ] == 0: commensalism (positive) amensalism (negative). metaW[, ] < 0: self-limitation (density dependence). Without , without negative interactions, abundances can grow without bound. Parameters kind matrix can generated random generateRandomGLVadjMat() (structure) generateGLVparmsFromAdj() (interaction strengths, r m).

title: meweasmo 0.3.0
text: metaWebNetAssemblyML(): multilayer version continuous-time metaweb assembly model. Non-trophic layers change extinction rates: species present positive effect (mutualism, commensalism) lowers extinction rate partner one negative effect (competition, amensalism) raises , e_i(t) = e_i exp(beta_neg f-_i - beta_pos f+_i), f fraction partners present (normalize = FALSE adds effects per partner instead). Optional obligate dependence (obligate_on, obligate_layers): dependent species go extinct rate se none species depend (e.g. foundation species) present. Takes mgraph list igraph layers, igraph layer attribute, edge data.frame; uses per-link sign attribute (effect_attr) present, otherwise layer signs default_layer_signs(). beta = 0 obligate rule metaWebNetAssemblyCT(). build_multilayer_assembly(): matrices multilayer model, check layers translated. metaWebNetAssemblyMLCT(): C++ core multilayer model (extinction rates simulated exactly thinning).
